metadata.title: U.S. AI-Related Stocks Extend Rally Premarket - WSJ

content.text:
0925 GMT – Stocks linked to the build-out in artificial intelligence continue to rally premarket. Investor confidence around AI returned in the last session following a selloff earlier this week. AI adoption still exceeds expectations, UBS analysts write, with signs of tight supply supporting the AI supply chain. Intel shares rise 2.3%, while chip-making peers Sandisk and Micron Technology MU 5.50%increase; up pointing triangle rise 1.6% and 1.1%, respectively. Power groups tied to the build-out in AI also gain premarket, with GE Vernova GEV -0.02%decrease; down pointing triangle and Caterpillar both up 1%. More broadly, Nasdaq futures rose 0.5%. (josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)
AI-Hit U.K. Tech Stocks Seen as Investment Opportunities
0731 GMT – Valuations for technology, media and telecom stocks in the U.K. still reflect concerns over artificial intelligence, but this means the sector offers attractive opportunities for investors, Berenberg analysts write in a note. “While the market has become slightly more discerning over the impact of AI, concern remains, reflected in still depressed valuations,” they say. Meeting market expectations, alongside with AI-driven growth and efficiency gains, should support a rerating, though it might take some time for this to happen, they say. (najat.kantouar@wsj.com)
